title: Anthropic Secures $45 Billion AI Compute Deal with Nscale to Boost Competitive Edge
summary: Anthropic has signed a $45 billion deal with British AI infrastructure company Nscale to rent advanced AI compute power using Nvidia’s Vera Rubin chips. The six-year agreement, set to begin in late 2027, is part of Anthropic’s aggressive strategy to expand its compute capacity and compete with rivals like OpenAI. This follows recent multi-billion-dollar deals with Volta, AMD, SpaceX, Amazon, Google, and Broadcom, reflecting the broader industry trend of securing massive compute resources for AI development.
key_points: Anthropic has signed a $45 billion deal with Nscale to rent AI compute power using Nvidia’s Vera Rubin chips, a state-of-the-art multi-chip system.
The six-year deal will supply compute capacity from Nscale’s flagship data center in West Virginia, starting in late 2027.
This is part of Anthropic’s aggressive compute expansion strategy to compete with OpenAI and other AI leaders.
Recent deals include $10 billion with Volta, $5 billion with AMD, $1.25 billion monthly capacity from SpaceX, and expanded partnerships with Amazon, Google, and Broadcom.
The AI industry is in a compute arms race, with major players like Google, OpenAI, and Meta also scaling up infrastructure.
